images.title: Shapes that stand for numbers
images.purpose: Shows an algebra grid of two rows with row sums 27 and 19, and the values of the square and circle.
images.composition: A 2 by 4 grid in the centre, and a small key of the two shapes to its right.
images.exact_structure: A grid of 2 rows and 4 columns of equal square cells, dark outlines. Row 1: three teal #0072B2 squares, then the sum 27 in the last cell. Row 2: two amber #E69F00 circles, one teal #0072B2 square, then the sum 19 in the last cell. The last column is shaded light grey to mark the sums. To the right, a small key of two lines: a teal square followed by = 9, and an amber circle followed by = 5. Nothing else is drawn. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, which is large and centred; no scenery, no people, no other text.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Solve the row with one kind of shape first, then use it in the next row.
images.description: Shows an algebra grid of two rows with row sums 27 and 19, and the values of the square and circle.
images.context: Picture for algebra grids with shapes.
images.teaching_notes: Three squares make 27 so a square is 9; then two circles make 10.

image_decisions.why: The grid itself is the problem; seeing the all square row shows where to start.
